newsitem.title: UK: London boat show sales jump to 59 million pounds.
newsitem.headline: London boat show sales jump to 59 million pounds.

text.p: Sales at the annual London International Boat Show, which ended on Sunday, jumped by 16 percent to 58.9 million pounds ($98.59 million), the organiser of the show said on Monday.

"Good reports came from all sectors of the market especially UK sailboat and powerboat builders with companies selling at levels not seen for many years, especially to the British consumer," trade association the British Marine Industries Federation (BMIF) said in a statement.

The federation said exhibitors at the show had reported excellent sales "with many companies reaching predicted business for the whole show within the first few days". The sales figure broke records for the second year running, it added.

Vessels ranged from huge powerboats such as the 1.8 million pound Sunseeker "Predator" to a six-foot long rowing dinghy called the Heyland Tadpole which cost only 297 pounds. A wide range of the latest in high-technology marine equipment such as that which helped solo British yachtsman Tony Bullimore survive the icy waters of the Southern Ocean was also on display.

Turnover for Britain's boating industry reached 1.88 billion pounds at the end of 1995 and the BMIF's chief executive Tony Beechey said recently there had been a healthy rise in sales in 1996, adding that the market was seen by many as a barometer for the economy in general.

The show's organisers blamed lower attendance figures at the show, 162,000 compared with 174,000 in 1996, on poor travelling conditions due to a cold spell of weather in Britain over the last two weeks.
